s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive pigmented lesion of the lip with local extension
salient_findings: Slowly enlarging pigmented lesion on the upper left lip vermilion
Brownish discoloration of the skin above the vermilion
Multiple pigmented papules of various sizes on the vermilion
key_facts: 4-year history of the lesion
Initial size of the lesion was 1 cm × 0.5 cm
Lesion progressively increased in size without symptoms
Brownish discoloration of the skin appeared after 3 years
No significant medical or family history
No smoking or drinking history
Multiple pigmented papules on the vermilion
Slightly swollen lip
Intraoral lesion with focal ulcerations
No cervical lymphadenopathy or other skin lesions
Normal complete blood count, biochemical profile, and urinalysis

shortlist.label: Malignant melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive pigmented lesion with focal ulcerations

shortlist.label: Mucosal melanoma of the lip
shortlist.why_kept: Intraoral lesion with local extension and pigmented papules

shortlist.label: Labial melanotic macule
shortlist.why_kept: Pigmented lesion on the lip vermilion with brownish discoloration

shortlist.label: Melanocytic nevus
shortlist.why_kept: Pigmented papules and lesion on the lip

shortlist.label: Laugier-Hunziker syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Pigmented lesions on the lip and oral mucosa

raw.rationale: The lesion's location on the lip vermilion and its intraoral extension are more consistent with mucosal melanoma, a subtype of malignant melanoma.

rejected.label: Malignant melanoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as the specific location and characteristics of the lesion suggest a more specific subtype.

rejected.label: Labial melanotic macule
rejected.why: Typically presents as a solitary, benign-appearing macule, which does not match the progressive and ulcerated nature of the lesion in this case.

rejected.label: Melanocytic nevus
rejected.why: Usually presents as a well-circumscribed, benign lesion, which does not fit the description of the lesion's progression and ulceration.

rejected.label: Laugier-Hunziker syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by multiple, benign-appearing macules, which does not match the malignant potential suggested by the lesion's progression and ulceration.
